what_it_does: Neuromorphic chips (brain-inspired processors that use 'spiking' signals rather than continuous numbers) are attractive for always-on edge devices like mobile robots. A known problem with any AI system is 'catastrophic forgetting' — when the model learns a new task, it overwrites what it knew before. One remedy is 'memory replay': periodically re-showing old data while learning new tasks. However, replay is expensive in energy and time because it requires many simulation steps to regenerate the spiking signals accurately. Replay4NCL compresses old knowledge into a compact form and replays it using far fewer simulation steps, cutting latency and energy substantially. To compensate for the information lost when using fewer steps, the method dynamically raises or lowers the threshold at which neurons 'fire' and adjusts the learning rate, keeping accuracy intact. Based on the abstract, this makes continual learning on spiking-neural-network (brain-inspired) chips practical for embedded devices.
